title: Smoky Black Bean Burger
summary: A hearty vegetarian burger with roasted black beans, warming spices and a crisp cheddar-topped crust, served with a quick-pickled onion and sriracha mayo.
equipment: large baking tray lined with baking paper

ingredients.item: tins black beans (400 g each), drained and rinsed
fine sea salt or table salt
small red onion, very thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
soft burger buns or brioche-style buns

steps.title: Dry-roast the beans
steps.text: Heat the oven to 180°C (160°C fan) and give it 20 minutes to come fully up to heat. Pat the black beans dry and spread them in a single layer on the lined tray, then bake at 180°C (160°C fan) for 15-20 minutes, until the skins start to split and the beans feel dry on the outside but are still soft within. Driving off this moisture is what stops the finished patties turning mushy; don't take them so far that they go hard and crunchy.

steps.title: Soften the vegetables
steps.text: Cook the onion and pepper in the olive oil over medium heat for 6-8 minutes until soft, then stir in the garlic, cumin and smoked paprika for 1 minute. Tip onto a plate lined with kitchen paper to soak up excess moisture and leave to cool slightly, so the hot vegetables don't start cooking the egg.

steps.title: Mix the burger mixture
steps.text: Mash the roasted beans roughly in a bowl, leaving about a third whole for texture, then mix in the softened vegetables, soy sauce, panko, egg, salt and pepper. The whole beans give bite, while the mash binds everything together.

steps.title: Shape and chill
steps.text: With wet hands, shape the mixture into 4 patties about 10cm wide and 2cm thick, then chill for 20 minutes. Chilling firms the patties so they hold together when they hit the hot pan.

steps.title: Quick-pickle the onion
steps.text: Toss the sliced red onion with lime juice and a pinch of salt and leave to pickle while you cook. The acidity softens the onion's sharp bite and turns it a vivid pink.

steps.title: Make the sriracha mayo
steps.text: Stir together mayo, sriracha, smoked paprika and lime juice in a small bowl. This spicy, citrusy sauce cuts through the earthiness of the beans.

steps.title: Fry the patties
steps.text: Heat 2 tablespoons of oil in a non-stick pan over medium heat and cook the patties for 4-5 minutes per side until deep brown and crisp, flipping gently with a fish slice as they're more delicate than beef. Add cheddar on top after flipping and cover for 1 minute to melt it; because the mixture contains egg, cook until the centre reaches 74°C.

steps.title: Toast the buns
steps.text: Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them cut-side down in a frying pan over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until golden. The toasted surface keeps the crumb from soaking up sauce and juices.

steps.title: Build the burger
steps.text: Spread the sriracha mayo on the bun, then layer lettuce, tomato, the cheesy patty and the pickled red onion. The pickled onion's sharpness lifts the whole burger.

tips: Don't skip drying the beans in the oven - this step gets rid of excess moisture and is what stops the patties turning mushy.
Chill the shaped patties for 20 minutes before cooking so they firm up and hold together in the pan.
Flip the patties gently with a fish slice, and not too early, as they're more delicate than beef until that first crust forms.
If the mixture feels too soft to shape, work in another 1-2 tablespoons of panko before chilling.

Frying safety: use a heavy, deep pot no more than half full of oil, with a clip-on thermometer, and dry the food before it goes in. Never leave hot oil unattended. If the oil catches fire, turn off the heat and cover the pot with a metal lid or use a fire extinguisher; never use water.
storage: Cooked patties keep in the fridge for up to 3 days, or freeze them cooked and cooled for up to 2 months. Reheat from chilled or frozen on a tray in a 180°C (160°C fan) oven for 10-20 minutes, until piping hot and 74°C in the centre, because the mixture contains egg. Cool leftovers in a shallow container and refrigerate within 2 hours (within 1 hour on a day above 32°C).
